answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with proof of unique knowledge. Each identity commits to a private knowledge base, and the network quizzes it on facts only that identity could hold, rejecting knowledge duplicated across identities. A fake farm cannot clone one mind into many, because each clone would fail the quiz. Like a tide that reveals a reef, the questions expose what is copied; like a trellis, the knowledge supports only the identity that grew it. Each extra fake needs its own distinct body of knowledge, a cost that cannot be shared, parallelized, or bought in bulk.
